_comment: Public replications gallery. One entry per independently contributed energy.json. Entries are added by the maintainer after a submission arrives as a GitHub issue on hongping-zh/ecocompute-mlcube; moderation checks schema and format only, never the numbers. Keep this list empty rather than seeded: a gallery of examples would be indistinguishable from fabricated replications.

_entry_schema.handle: contributor handle as they want to be credited, e.g. @someone
_entry_schema.arch: one of turing | ada | ampere | blackwell | hopper | volta
_entry_schema.n: independent trials, integer >= 1 (declared by the contributor; the container's iterations are not trials)
_entry_schema.report: URL to the raw energy.json, or null
_entry_schema.link: repo / blog / paper URL, or null
_entry_schema.note: maintainer's one-line reading of the point, or null

entries.gpu: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050 Ti Laptop GPU
entries.note: First independent replication - thank you. NF4 saves 16.2% here, while every card we own spends 4.6-33% more at this size; the fitted Ampere curve is extrapolated ~6x below its measured range (7-14B) at 1.1B, so its band there is too wide to test anything. The paired perplexity, 10.1016 against an FP16 9.6201, matches our own RTX 4090 measurement of the same model to four decimals - same weights, same corpus, different machine and OS.

First Volta-architecture data point, and the second independent replicator overall. NF4 saves 1.7% on a V100S at 1.1B - same sign as the Ampere-laptop result above (-16.2%) at the same model, and opposite to every fitted consumer curve (Ada/Blackwell spend 4.6-33% more at this size). Volta has no fitted curve yet, so this point stands on its own as pure measurement.
The strongest saving of the three Volta runs (-7.9% at 3B). Note the paired perplexity damage (+27.6%) is large - the energy saving is real but the quality trade-off is part of the honest picture.

NF4 still saves energy at 7B on V100S. Three sizes, three savings: on this bandwidth-constrained datacenter card NF4 pays off at every measured size, while our Ada/Blackwell cards spend more energy below ~2-7B - the bandwidth-starvation hypothesis gains its first architecture-class-level support from an external contributor.
